title: Türkiye's Digital Nomad Visa: Who Qualifies and How to Apply, Step by Step
excerpt: The 36 eligible nationalities, the USD 3,000-a-month rule and the other requirements, then the three steps: the online certificate, the consulate visa and the six-month residence permit.
bodyHtml:
Türkiye's Digital Nomad program lets eligible remote workers come with a dedicated visa and then apply for a six-month residence permit. It is three separate steps with three separate authorities, and most confusion comes from mixing them up. This guide walks through each one.

It is practical information from the official program pages, not legal advice. Requirements can change, and each consulate sets its own visa checklist, so confirm your case with the mission that handles your application.

How it works: three steps

  1. Digital Nomad Identification Certificate — an online application to the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, which checks whether you qualify as a digital nomad.

  2. Digital nomad visa — with that certificate, you apply at a Turkish consulate or visa application center.

  3. Short-term residence permit — once you're in Türkiye on that visa, you can apply through e-İkamet for a six-month short-term residence permit for tourism purposes, within the visa period.

The certificate is not a visa, and the visa is not a residence permit. Each step can be refused on its own.

Check you qualify before you start

Nationality. Only citizens of these 36 countries can apply:

  • EU: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden

  • Rest of Europe: Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, United Kingdom, Belarus, Russian Federation, Ukraine

  • North America: United States, Canada

Cyprus is the one EU country not on the list, and there are no countries from Asia, Africa, Latin America or Oceania. If yours isn't listed, the program isn't open to you — check our guide to entering Türkiye for your other options.

The other requirements:

  • Aged 21 to 55

  • A university degree (a diploma or degree certificate)

  • A passport valid for at least six months from the date you arrive in Türkiye

  • Income of at least USD 3,000 a month, or USD 36,000 a year

  • Remote work for a company outside Türkiye: an employment contract if you're an employee, or a business contract with a client company if you're self-employed. Contracts with companies located in Türkiye don't count.

Step 1: the certificate

Sign up on the GoTürkiye Digital Nomads platform and upload scans of:

  1. Your passport (valid six months from arrival)

  2. Your diploma or degree certificate

  3. Your employment contract, or your business contract with a client company — neither with a company in Türkiye

  4. A biometric photo

  5. A document proving income of USD 3,000 a month or USD 36,000 a year

The platform reviews the documents and, if they're sufficient, assigns you a certificate. It doesn't publish a list of acceptable income proof, so upload something that clearly shows the amount, the period and your name. Questions about this step go to the Ministry at nomad@ktb.gov.tr.

Step 2: the visa

Take the certificate to the Turkish consulate or visa application center that handles applications from where you live, together with whatever else that mission asks for. Document lists, fees and appointment waits vary by mission, so get the checklist from them before you book — not from a blog post or someone else's experience in another country.

Step 3: the residence permit

Once you enter Türkiye on the digital nomad visa, you can apply through e-İkamet for a six-month short-term residence permit for tourism purposes. Apply within your visa period — not after it ends.

Two things to sort out before you apply:

  • Health insurance that covers the whole permit period and is accepted by the migration authority. See our guide to health insurance for your residence permit.

  • An address you can register, since the permit application needs one.

An application is not an approval. Applications are finalized within 90 days at the latest, and your provincial migration directorate may ask for more documents. Questions go to the Foreigners Communication Center, YİMER 157.

What it doesn't cover

  • Working for Turkish employers or clients. The program is for remote work for companies abroad. Local employment generally needs a work permit or a formal exemption.

  • Tax. The visa says nothing about where you pay tax. Staying more than six months in a calendar year can make you a Turkish tax resident.

  • Staying indefinitely. The official pages describe a six-month permit. Don't assume it renews automatically — ask the migration authority before you plan a longer stay.

Our guide to working remotely from Türkiye covers work permits, tax residence and social security in detail.

Do you even need it?

Many of the 36 eligible nationalities can already visit Türkiye without a visa for a limited stay. If your trip fits inside that, you may not need this program at all. It earns its paperwork when you want a longer, documented stay as a remote worker. Check your own entry rules in our guide to entering Türkiye first.

Before you apply

  • Your nationality is on the list, and you're between 21 and 55.

  • You have your degree certificate scanned.

  • Your passport runs at least six months past your arrival date.

  • Your contract is with a company outside Türkiye.

  • You can prove USD 3,000 a month or USD 36,000 a year.

  • You have the consulate's own checklist for step 2.

  • You've lined up accepted health insurance and an address for step 3.
